content: 1. Administer 2 grams of valacyclovir orally every 12 hours for 1 day, followed by 1 gram orally every 8 hours for 7 days. Note that there is no data on efficacy if treatment is initiated more than 72 hours after the onset of the rash. 2. For an initial episode, administer 1 gram of valacyclovir orally every 12 hours for 10 days. 3. For recurrent episodes, administer 500 milligrams of valacyclovir orally every 12 hours for 3 days. Efficacy is not established if treatment begins more than 24 hours after lesion onset. 4. For suppressive therapy in immunocompetent patients, administer 1 gram of valacyclovir orally per day. 5. For suppressive therapy in immunocompetent patients with ≤9 recurrences annually, administer 500 milligrams of valacyclovir orally per day. For transmission reduction to a source partner, administer 500 milligrams orally per day. 6. For suppressive therapy in HIV-infected patients, administer 500 milligrams of valacyclovir orally every 12 hours. 7. In children under 2 years of age, the safety and efficacy of valacyclovir have not been established. For children over 2 years, administer 20 milligrams per kilogram orally every 8 hours for 5 days, not exceeding 1 gram per dose. 8. In children under 12 years of age, the safety and efficacy of valacyclovir have not been established. For those over 12 years, administer 2 grams orally every 12 hours for 1 day. 9. Monitor renal function closely, as dosage adjustments may be necessary depending on renal status. 10. Valacyclovir and bacitracin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. 11. Avoid concurrent use of bacitracin with other nephrotoxic drugs, including valacyclovir and imipenem/cilastatin, as the mechanism is unknown. Co-administration may increase the risk of seizures. Avoid unless the potential benefit outweighs the risk. 12. Valacyclovir decreases the effects of talimogene laherparepvec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Antiviral agents may interfere with the effectiveness of talimogene laherparepvec. 13. Cimetidine increases valacyclovir levels by reducing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. 14. Co-administration of valacyclovir with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. 15. Co-administration of emtricitabine or tenofovir with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase serum concentrations of these drugs. Monitor closely. 16. Valacyclovir increases the levels of emtricitabine and tenofovir DF. Use with caution and monitor closely. 17. Ublituximab decreases the effects of valacyclovir through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use with caution and monitor closely. 18. Probenecid increases valacyclovir levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is considered minor, but its significance is unknown. 19. Valacyclovir increases the effects of zidovudine through an unknown mechanism. This interaction is considered minor, but its significance is unknown. Monitor for lethargy and fatigue. 20. Valacyclovir has a half-life of approximately 3 hours, while acyclovir has a half-life of 14–20 hours in end-stage renal disease. The drug is primarily excreted in the urine (89%) and minimally in feces. 21. For breastfeeding mothers, consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother’s clinical need for therapy and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child from the drug or the underlying maternal condition. There is no data on the effects of valacyclovir on breastfed children or milk production. 22. Valacyclovir is generally considered acceptable during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. 23. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only.
